capabilities: Group each pane's open tabs into an automatically tracked, nameable group
Hide or complete groups to tuck panes away or close them while keeping tab lists restorable
File groups into collapsible sections per timeframe, sprint, or deadline and hide whole sections
Colour-code panes and sidebar rows with per-group and per-section overrides
Search, reorder, and move tabs between groups with keyboard navigation
disambiguation: Not a tab-layout tool; it explicitly does not arrange panes in columns or scroll, it groups tabs by task and timeframe.
extras: Terminal tab groups can't be restored after an Obsidian restart because the underlying processes don't survive restarts; note groups reopen by file path. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: Inspired by Workona, built for Obsidian.
motivation: The author saw existing tab tools solving a layout problem (columns, scroll) when the real need is grouping tabs by task and hiding finished work to reclaim screen space.
problem: Obsidian organizes notes by folders and links, but nothing captures which currently open tabs belong together as in-progress work or belong to a current timeframe.

relations.evidence: Inspired by Workona, built for Obsidian.
If you run terminals in your vault — say with Terminus — they pile up fast

summary: Sidebar panel that groups open tabs (from any pane, including plugin views) into named, hideable groups and timeframe sections you complete when done.
